title: Le Blanc holds the latter — grace-persuasion presupposes faith already in the heart
source_text: C. Et nos quoque Thesibus editis annis superioribus posteriorem illam sententiam amplexi sumus, & omnino tenendam esse existimamus. Quod enim ista fiducia qua quis certo statuit, & sibi persuadet, se Deo esse reconciliatum, & ab eo per Christum in gratiam receptum, non sit actus fidei primarius & essentialis, sed solum secundarius atque accidentalis, evidenter probari & demonstrari potest. Quippe nemo potest istud vere & legitime sibi persuadere, & apud se certo statuere, quin prius in se animum reflectens, & propriam conscientiam discutens atque examinans, veram vivamque fidem, ex contentis ejus in Scriptura notis, in se agnoverit atque perceperit. Nam talis persuasio, absque revelatione quadam speciali & extraordinaria, vera esse non potest, quin sit conclusio talis Syllogismi, Qui credit in Christum fide viva & operante per dilectionem Deo reconciliatus est, & ab eo per Christum in gratiam receptus. At dum ego propriam conscientiam excutio, agnosco in me talem fidem. Ergo sum Deo reconciliatus, & ab eo per Christum in gratiam receptus. Ac proinde haec persuasio praesupponit fidem jam in corde existentem, & sic non potest ejus essentiam constituere.
pass_a_gloss: And we also in Theses published in former years embraced that latter opinion, and judge that it is altogether to be held. For that that trust by which one certainly lays down, and persuades himself, that he is reconciled to God, and received by him into grace through Christ, is not a primary and essential act of faith, but only secondary and accidental, can be evidently proved and demonstrated. Inasmuch as no one can truly and legitimately persuade himself of that, and certainly lay it down with himself, unless first reflecting upon himself, and discussing and examining his own conscience, he has acknowledged and perceived in himself true and living faith from the notes of it contained in Scripture. For such persuasion, apart from some special and extraordinary revelation, cannot be true unless it is the conclusion of such a Syllogism: Whoever believes in Christ with a living faith working through love is reconciled to God, and received by him into grace through Christ. But while I examine my own conscience, I acknowledge such faith in myself. Therefore I am reconciled to God, and received by him into grace through Christ. And accordingly this persuasion presupposes faith already existing in the heart, and so cannot constitute its essence.
pass_b_english: Le Blanc’s earlier theses already took the Perkins–Ames side — and he still holds it.
Persuasion that I am reconciled and received into grace is secondary/accidental, not primary/essential.
Without special revelation it is only the conclusion of a syllogism: living faith working through love → reconciled; I find such faith in myself → therefore reconciled.
So the persuasion presupposes faith already in the heart — it cannot be faith’s essence.
